<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>I</c>ubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.

<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.

<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Exsultémus Dómino.

<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>L</c>et us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

<r>Osee 2:1-3</r>

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uintodécimo Kaléndas Decémbris Luna séptima. Anno Dómini 2026
<h>N</h>eocæsaréæ, in Ponto, natális sancti Gregórii, Epíscopi et Confessóris, doctrína et sanctitáte illústris, qui propter signa atque mirácula, quæ cum multa Ecclesiárum glória perpetrávit, Thaumatúrgus est appellátus.
<h>H</h>elpíthi, in Saxónia, item natális sanctæ Gertrúdis, Vírginis, ex Ordine sancti Benedícti, quæ dono revelatiónum clara éxstitit. Ipsíus tamen festívitas prídie huius diéi celebrátur.
<h>I</h>n Palæstína sanctórum Mártyrum Alphǽi et Zachǽi, qui primo anno persecutiónis Diocletiáni, post multa torménta, capitálem senténtiam subiére.
<h>C</h>órdubæ, in Hispánia, sanctórum Mártyrum Acíscli et Victóriæ germanórum, qui, in eádem persecutióne, Diónis Prǽsidis iussu sævíssime cruciáti sunt, et illústri passióne corónas a Dómino meruérunt.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ sancti Dionýsii Epíscopi, summæ eruditiónis viri, qui, multis confessiónibus clarus et pro passiónum tormentorúmque diversitáte magníficus, plenus diérum Conféssor quiévit, Valeriáni et Galliéni Imperatórum tempóribus.
<h>A</h>ureliánis, in Gállia, sancti Aniáni Epíscopi, cuius mortem in conspéctu Dómini pretiósam mirácula crebra testántur.
<h>I</h>n Británnia sancti Hugónis Epíscopi, qui, ex Mónacho Carthusiáno ad Ecclésiam Lincolniénsem regéndam vocátus, multis cláruit miráculis, et sancto fine quiévit.
<h>T</h>urónis, in Gállia, sancti Gregórii Epíscopi.
<h>F</h>loréntiæ sancti Eugénii Confessóris, qui fuit Diáconus beáti Zenóbii, eiúsdem civitátis Epíscopi.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.803e8415f6:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>N</c>ovember 17th 2026, the 7th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Neo-Caesarea, in Pontus, (about the year 270,) holy Gregory, Archbishop of that see, who was famous for teaching and holiness, and who came to be called the Wonder-worker, on account of the great signs and wonders which he worked to the great glory of the churches.
<h>A</h>t Helfta, in Saxony, (in the year 1334,) the holy Virgin Gertrude, of the Order of St. Benedict, eminent for her gift of revelations, whose feast is kept upon the day before.
<h>I</h>n Palestine, the holy martyrs Alphaeus and Zacchaeus, who were put to death after suffering many torments, in the first year of the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.
<h>A</h>t Cordova, the holy brother and sister Acisclus and Victoria, both martyrs, who in the same persecution by Diocletian aforesaid, were most cruelly tortured by command of the President Dion, and earned crowns of glory from the hand of the Lord.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, holy Denys, Bishop (of that see,) a man of great learning, and glorious on account of his many confessions and his diverse sufferings and torments, who at length fell asleep in the Lord, full of days but still a Confessor, in the time of the Emperors Valerian and Gallienus, (in the year 265.)
<h>A</h>t Orleans, (in the year 453,) holy Anian, Bishop (of that see,) the preciousness of whose death, in the sight of the Lord, is attested by many miracles.
<h>I</h>n England, holy Hugh, Bishop of Lincoln. He was a Charter House Monk, who was called to rule the Church of Lincoln, was famous for many miracles, and died an holy death, (in the year 1200.)
<h>A</h>t Tours, (in the year 595,) holy Gregory, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Florence, the holy Confessor Eugene, a Deacon of blessed Zenobius, Bishop of that see.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
